DEATH 011 "CAPTAIN " MATHER. Mr. William Mather, better known as "Captain" Mather, died art an early hour on Wednesday morn- ing, at his residence in Butterinarket-street. The deceased gentlemsh was 74 years of age last Decem- ber, and was well known and much respected. He was one of those who, commencing at a compara- tively low rung of the ladder of life, work them- selves up by industry and thrift to a position of comfort and independence. After working at his trade for some time he became landlord of the Lower Angel Inn, in Buttermarket-street, and on retiring from business life he went to live at Elles- mere Port, but subsequently returned to Warring- ton, where he has since resided in Buttemarket- street. He was well known for his fondness of boating, fishing, sailing, and shooting, and this causiod him to be known by the title of "Captain." It will be remembered that on the 29th of last month deceased and the late Inspector Berry, of the Borough Police Force, went on a shooting expedi- tion, on the river Mersey, and that, when returning, the boat in which the couple were came into colli- sion with a flat and capsized. The Inspector was drowneg, and Mr. Mather was with some difficulty rescued. He was then in an exhausted condition, and was in a delicate state of health up to the time of his demise. It is supposed that his death was hastened by the exposure he then experienced, and the shock to the system that he received.

WARRINGTON lIIUNAJPAL EL!*C- TIONS. Considerable controversy has during the past few days; taken place with regard to the action to be taken to fill up the vacancies in the Town Council of Warrington, caused by the retirement of those memberWwhose term of office expires with the close of the prtsent municipal year. The retiring Coun- cillors are :—Liberals Messrs. John Plate, Charles; Broadben‘ John Brown, and John Greening;. Con- servatives: Messrs. Richard Walker Francomb, James Cave Whittle, Thomas Jolley, Thomas Nitton, and William Tinsley. Fraill this itwill be seen that four Liberal members and five Conservative item- 'hers retire. Last week several Party meetings were held to consider the subject, but, although endea- vours were made to come to an amicable under- standing on the matter, no satisfactory conclusion, was arrived at, said it is even yet uncertain what - action will be taken. Writing under date the 15t111 October to Mr. John Crosfieldt, as representing the' Liberal Association, Mr. A Re:molds said that the Council of the Conservative Association the previous evening passed a resolution that unless the Liberals gave them (the Conservatives) a seat ki the North-West and North-East-Wards they were prepared to, and intended to, contest those wards at the forthcoming municipal elections. There would, the letter said, be another meeting of the Council the following day, when, if there were no amicable terms, candidates would be selected for the•contest. This, of course, indicatedthe desire on the part of the Conservative party to. increase tbeirpresent majority on the Town Council by two seats, and the proposal was naturally, as -we stated in our last issue, received with the utmost disfa- vour by the Liberal party. At a meeting of Con- servatives held on Saturday evening,. we under- stand; a decision was come to that the -Alole- of the wards should be contested, and the following gen- tlemen were chosen as Conservative candidates:-- North4-East Ward, Messrs. R: Heaton and W. D• Jeans;; North-West, Messrs. J. Smethurs- and T. Robinson;;South-East, Councillor Francomb and Mr. J. V-Taylor ; South-West, Councillors Sutton. and Jolley.; Latchford Ward, Councillor Tinsley.:. Owing to the letter above mentioned, indlcatin. g the attitude of their political opponentN. the LiberalScalled an aggregate meeting of Ward'Cora- mittees, of the Liberal Association, whicli) was, held on Monday evening in Wycliffe,- Hen, Bewseystreet, under the presidency et' Mr. J. G. McMinnies, the object being to consider-the• offer made to, them, and to further deliberate- on what stepsslion sfren. It was considered the meeting;thatthe demands of the Conservatives practically amounted to an insult, as the onlylob- jection that could be raised against the rething: J.,iberal Councillors was a political one, and the -fol- lowing resolution was unanimously arrived ' at- " That the whole- of the Liberal members of 'tlit:v ' Town Council be requested to resign their seats as,a public protest against the insult offered to -the- Liberal party...in theborough by the proposal of the Conservatlie- Associntion in reference to the ensu- ing municipal elections." Since then, it is stated,. the leaders of the Conservative party have made some effort to 'induce their party to agree to main- tain the statics quo; which practically means an assent to the proposal' of the Liberal party. It is% stated that, Mr. W.. IL Jeans and Mr. T. Robinson,. two of the Conservative nominees, have intimated their decision to withdraw, but we understand that Mr. Robert Heaton and Mr. Smethurst, having in• . the first instance been requested to stand for the- North-East and: North-West Wards respectively;, have now declined to retire; and threaten to come • out as independent candidates if not supported by: their party. Mr. J. Cave Whittle (Conservative); • who has sat for the South-East Ward. has not again: ' been nominated by his party, but it is alleged that he intends to contest the ward on his own accoun, against the Conservative nominees, Mr. It. W. Fran comb and Mr. J.. V. Taylor. We understand that the whole of the fourteen Liberal members of the • Council are pledged to retire should the extreme policy of their opponents be persisted in. Mondayr next, it may be,adde.dris, the nomination day.

div.head: ATTEMPTED SUICIDE OF A BANK MANAGER.
div.p: ATTEMPTED SUICIDE OF A BANK MANAGER.

On Wednesday morning the circulation of a ru- mour in Warrington, thai; Mr. John Ellison, the esteemed manager of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Bank, in Horsemarket-street, had attempted suicide, caused a sorrowful sensation. On inquiry it was found that the rumour was unfortunately true. From what can-be learned, it appears that between eight and nine o'Clock on Wednesday morning, Mr. Ellison, who lives in Wilson Patten-street, was found in his bedroom, lying in a pool of blood, which had issued from a severe wound in the throat. Medical assistance was obtained without delay. and everything possible was done for the sufferer, whose life was' despaired of. On Wednes- day night he was somewhat better, and he has since lingered in a critical condition, but only faint hopes are as yet entertained of his ultimate recoverg. C+2eat sympathy is expressed on all sides for the un- fortunate gentleman and his- family, especially as the act is solely attributed to, an unhinged state of mind. Mr. Ellison's health has for some time been in an unsatisfactory state,. and it is stated that he should have gone to Southport,. with a view to r - cruiting it, on the day the-sad act was committed. He is a native of Warringtbn,whothas gained the high regard of all who have come in contact with him, either in private life or in the clurse of business, and it need hardly be said thathis unfortunate posi- tion is much deplored.

WARRINGTON, 22ND OCTOBRR, 1886. DEAR Srus, GREENALL, BARONET, V. WALKER A: CO. An action having been commenced by Sir Gilbert Greenall. Baronet, against our client as editor of The Warrington Examiner, in consequence of the following editorial remarks contained in that paper on the 17th July la,t "More evidence of the part drink has played on the side of the Tories in the Warrington Election. Two men brought up at the Police Court, on Monday, for being drunk and dis- orderly the day after the election, admitted that they were supplied with the liquor at Wilderspool, and that they had been drinking out of buckets. Could anything be more dis- graceful to the Tory candidate and the firm with which he is connected? What of the Corrupt Practices Act? I, it an offence to give a glass of beer before the election, but per- fectly legal to supply liquor in buckets after the election ? These are questions which ought' to be answered in a court of law. If Sir Gilbert Greenall and his henchmen are lacking in re4ard for decericy, would it not be as well to try and make them imolai by Act of Parliament? On the very day these poor wretches were being fitted for the police court by being deluged at Wilderspool, with Wilderspool Ale, the brewer of Virilderspool was returning thanks at the Conservative Club for his election, and asking his hearers itolet them in their daily life and conduct try to honour God.' What a mockery! To quote the elegant language ot Lord Salisbury, It is a wonder the words didn't choke him." We are initructed to say that the inquiries our client has made have satisfied him tnat the statements at the Borough Police Court. upon which his remarks were based, are, and always were, without the slightest foundation. We therefore, on his behalf, at once and unreservedly with• draw the remarks, expressing his deep regret that they should have been published, and we further consent to the payment by him of all costs on further proceedings in the action being stayed. We are, yours truly, RIDGWAY AND WORBLEY. Messrs. RODELET DAvIES, SHARD, AND ICIRECONExL.

LYMM LOCAL BOARD.—NOTICE TO DAIRYMEN, COWKEEPERS, AND PURVEYORS OF MILS. The Contagious Diseases (Animals) Acts, 1878 and 1888. The Dairies, Covesheds. and Milkshops' Order of 1885. Pursuant to the above mentioned order of the Privy Council made the 15th day of June, 1885, under the Contagious Dis- eases (Animals) Act, 1879, and pursuant to the provisions of the Contagions Diseases (Animals) Act. 1886, We, the Local Authority for the District of LyMm, in the County of Chester, do HEREBY GIVE PUBLIC NOTICE that a register is now open for the Registration, under the said Ordcr, of all persons from time to time carrying on within the said district the trades of Cowkeepers. Dairymen, or Purveyors of Milk. The mode of Registration is as follows : Every Dairyman, Cowkeeper. and Putveyor of Milk shall make written application to the Law Clerk to be Registered, and shall describe in such applica- tion, his trade, and the situation, number, and dimensions of the buildings and premises in respect of which he applies to be registered. When the application la filled up in the pre- scribed manner, it must be forwarded to the Law Clerk, at the Board Office, Pepper-street, Lymm, and upon the Board being satisfied that the requirements of the Order and of the Notice of the Local Authority have been complied with. the Law Clerk shalt forthwith register the same in the register for that purpose, and shall trarsmit to the applicant a certificate of the Registration tjaereof. Forms of application will be supplied free of charge to any applicant, end may be obtained at the Board Office. AND NOTICE IS ALSO HEREBY GIVEN, that it is not lawful for any person to carry on in the said district the trade of a COwkeeper. Dairyman, or Purveyor of Milk, unless he is regis- tered as such under the said Order. Dated this 2uth day of October, 1886. T. J. RIDGWAY, Law Clerk. BOROUGH OF ST. HELENS. TO THE BUR- GESSES OF HARDSHAW WARD. LAtIES AND GENTLEMEN,—The Town Council having this day done me the honour of electing me to the offise of Alder- man for this borougb. I have to wi, hdraw from my candidature at the forthcoming election of a councillor for your ward. I take this opportunity of again thanjking you for the con- fidence you have reposed in me in the past and for your kind expressions of approval of my conduct as one of your repre sentatives in the Town Council. I am, ladies and gentlemen, Your obedient Servant, DUNCAN MCICECHNIE. Laurel-road, St. Ann's, *a 20 h Oct., 1886. BOROUGH—OF ST. HELENS.EIT—R- GESSES OF EAST SUTTON WARD. LADIES AND GENTLEItEN,—My term f office as your repre- sentative will expire in a few days. I have faithfully en- deavoured to represent your interest and discharge the duties Imposed upon me as a member of the Town Council. I have been requested by many and irfluential residents of the ward to again represent your ward. In deference to this mark of continued confidence in me, I again consent to become a candidate at the forthcoming election, and should I be re- elected, I shall, to the best of my ability, attend to the in- terests of your ward and those of the borough generally. Thanking you for your former support and soliciting a renewal of it, I remain, Ladies and gentlemen. Your obedient servant, JAMES FISHER. Olive Mount, Mill-lane, Sutton, Oct. 14th, 1886.
